OWNER SPECIFICATION REVIEW EVENT, r11 Part A (the ten-row owner packet), 2026-09-16.
Recorded under the r11 closure mandate's AFK review authority on an explicit owner ruling,
transcribed verbatim in work/r11-campaign/RULINGS-OWNER-10.md. This is a CLAIM CORRECTION:
the registry is brought to what the code already does, and no implementation was weakened.

RULING (row 1, R11-355, filed high / adjudicated medium): ACCEPT the correction; the code is
right.

WHAT MOVED: the `statement`. It enumerated the states in which the signer yields nothing and
ended "...and when its snapshot lock is poisoned".

WHY THAT WAS FALSE. `DelegatedServerSigner::current` recovers a poisoned read guard with
`unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner())` (delegated_server_signer/mod.rs:209-212)
and then applies only `now < a.exp` (mod.rs:213-216). The protected value is one
`Option<Arc<..>>` swapped whole, so no partially mutated invariant can become visible and a
poisoned lock yields exactly the verdict a healthy one yields. The theorem's own registered
control asserted the opposite of the theorem: it asserted `signer.current(NOW).is_some()`
and `seconds_to_expiry(NOW) == Some(300)` under a genuinely poisoned lock. The module note at
mod.rs:109-116 argues FOR recovery at length, so the code is deliberate and the text was the
defect.

WHY RECOVERY IS THE SAFER DESIGN, and why this does not weaken the claim. Failing closed on
poison would let one unrelated panic anywhere in the process permanently retire this
replica's signing — a self-inflicted outage triggerable by any bug in any other subsystem.
The statement now says terminal retirement DOMINATES every later read and publication, that
poison is recovered because the protected snapshot is whole-value state whose invariant is
preserved across unwind, and that recovery overrides neither terminal retirement nor
expiration. Every state in which the signer yields nothing is unchanged except the one that
never existed.

TAKEN WITH IT: the control was renamed from
`a_poisoned_snapshot_lock_fails_closed_and_still_recovers` to
`a_poisoned_snapshot_lock_is_recovered_and_retirement_still_dominates`, which is what its
body has always asserted. The old name is what made the false conjunct look supported at a
glance.

MEASURED AND UNCHANGED: the contract packet's G4. The row as filed asked for it to be
reworded; the adjudication read the source and ruled otherwise — "fails closed rather than
panicking inside a request future" reads as *the fail-closed decision is still made from what
the guard holds, without a panic*, and G4's second clause already says the replica can retire
and re-publish. `security_consequence` and `scope` needed no change; neither mentions poison.
subject: THM-0062
